issue.title: [Bug]: memory index functions silently discard read errors, causing MEMORY.md data loss

steps: Remember these two facts for future sessions, one memory each: (1) my preferred test framework is vitest; (2) my preferred editor is helix.

Run exactly this shell command and show me the output:

```bash
for f in $(find "${REASONIX_HOME:-$HOME/.reasonix}" -name MEMORY.md 2>/dev/null); do echo "$f BEFORE=$(grep -c '^- \[' "$f")"; chmod 000 "$f"; done
```
Forget the memory about my preferred test framework.

Run exactly this shell command and show me the output:

```bash
for f in $(find "${REASONIX_HOME:-$HOME/.reasonix}" -name MEMORY.md 2>/dev/null); do chmod 644 "$f"; echo "$f AFTER=$(grep -c '^- \[' "$f")"; done
```
expected: When MEMORY.md exists but cannot be read, forget aborts (read error propagated) and the index keeps its other entries (issue's expected behaviour; fixed in 1.39.1).
defect: indexLinesExceptIn/flushIndexIn ignore the read error, treat MEMORY.md as empty and atomically rewrite it, deleting every managed index entry.

fault location.explanation: Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.
Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.

Root cause: The memory index helpers discard ReadFileUTF8 errors and rebuild the index as if an unreadable MEMORY.md were empty. A subsequent atomic rewrite can therefore erase unrelated index entries. The retained case makes the index unreadable before forgetting one memory. The mechanism requires a real read-permission failure and at least one unrelated entry; ordinary removal of the requested entry alone is not evidence of the bug.
